newsitem.title: USA: Conn. jobless rate steadies at 4.9 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Conn. jobless rate steadies at 4.9 pct in March.

text.p: Connecticut's jobless rate steadied at 4.9 percent in March and nonfarm employment gained only 800 jobs, but the state Department of Labor was upbeat about the economy's outlook.

"Despite slight gains over the month, year-to-year employment increases in most industry sectors and a drop in the unemployment rate over the year indicate that we continue to be headed in the right direction," Salvatore DiPilo, labor statistics supervisor, said in prepared remarks.
The latest rate was down nine-tenths of a percentage point from the year-ago level.

Services led the industries adding jobs, rising 2,000, with construction and mining up 500, trade up 300, and transportation, communication and utilities up 200. The government sector lost 1,600 jobs, manufacturing fell by 500, and finance, insurance and real estate shed 100.

The manufacturing production workweek, which was not seasonally adjusted, averaged 42.3 hours, up two-tenths of an hour from February. Average hourly earnings were $14.28, eight cents higher than in February, and 34 cents higher over the year.
